answer: Sybil resistance works by forcing each agent to lock collateral as an anchor in a shared identity ledger. Every vote is signed by that anchor, so splitting into fakes only divides one stake: influence per identity shrinks while the operator still pays lockup and fees for each. Peer attestations act as a prism, separating genuine agents from clones that reuse the same funding or behavior; clones rushing to the summit together reveal the shared pattern. To pose as N agents, an attacker must post N independent stakes and grow N uncorrelated histories, so cost scales with N, not one identity.
